summary: An errored Claude Code result event now fails the run and transient failures are classified retryable, so agent-step's existing retry loop absorbs a dropped connection instead of burning the phase on no_result; all four gates green.

plan_deviations: The plan's word-boundary mitigation for bare status codes (F1b) was wrong — \b500\b does match 'processed 500 files'. My own guard test caught it on the first run. I fixed the pattern to require an error context rather than deleting the test; it also matches the real 'API Error: 429 {...}' shape the CLI emits.
Skipped the planned claude-stream-error.ndjson fixture — classification needs one event, so a literal object in the table test plus a mock CLI is clearer coverage than a file nobody opens.

Found and fixed a stale doc claim (salvage is now conditional on the result event reporting success) that no prior phase flagged. The plugin docs turned out to be bundled into src/cli/bundled/plugin-docs.ts and byte-compared by a unit test, so docs:bundle had to run.
details.verification: Mutation-tested the fix: removing the retry guard (1 test fails), ignoring is_error (5 fail), and forcing retryable:false (2 fail) each break the suite — the coverage is real, not decorative.
details.known_accepted_regression: A run that now fails no longer reaches emitAgentCost, so its spend leaves the cost ledger (plan's F3). Carrying spend on a failure would need a public_api change to the adapter error contract. Documented in the plugin's Limitations rather than left silent; the status quo was strictly worse — it booked a failed run as a successful $2.28 AND burned the phase.
details.out_of_scope: Gemini CLI and OpenCode share the defect class but were not fixed — no live evidence of their error shapes, and a test against a guessed shape proves nothing. Session resume for a cut-off run belongs to #34.
